column2: req_desc

Keyboard-built automation
An Automation builder takes a new form automation from an empty canvas to a published version using only the keyboard, and a visitor's submission then runs it to success with the email visible in Mailpit.

Grid cursor and focus landing
Arrow keys move the grid cursor, the published letter keys add each step kind at the cursor, and focus lands on the published element after every canvas action in the keyboard table.

Step settings dialog focus
Enter on a step opens its settings dialog with focus inside it, Tab and Shift+Tab wrap within the dialog, and Escape or the close button returns focus to the step.

Publish creates a numbered version
Publish copies the draft into the next immutable numbered version, makes it live, refuses when nothing changed, and announces the new version in the Run updates region.

Send-email confirmed by the mail server
A send-email step becomes succeeded only after Mailpit has accepted the message, and the accepted message carries the published From, run-id header, templated subject and templated body.

Public form intake
A public form validates its published fields, starts exactly one run of the live version with the submitted values as trigger output, and answers not found when the automation has no live version.

Pointer-built automation
An Automation builder drags steps onto the grid, wires them by dragging between ports, and meets the cycle and disconnected-step refusals in one pointer session.

Pointer placement and wiring
A dropped or moved step snaps to the nearest grid cell and cannot share a cell, and only a drag from an output port to another step's input port draws an edge.

Edge drawing motion
A newly drawn edge reports data-anim running while it draws in and none afterwards, and reports none throughout when the user prefers reduced motion.

Save refusals for edges
Saving an edge that would close a cycle, give a step a second incoming edge, or end at the trigger is refused with the published message and draws nothing.

Publish refusals move focus
Publish refuses each published invalid draft condition with its exact message and step id, and focus moves to that step on the canvas or in the step list.

Opposite ports on two manual runs
A builder runs a published branch twice from the Run now control with different inputs, and the run details show opposite ports taken with the untaken part skipped.

Condition comparison rules
Filter and branch conditions compare as numbers when both sides parse as numbers and as case-sensitive strings otherwise, with the published operators and worked examples.

Template typing
A template field that is one whole expression keeps the value's type, any other field becomes a string, and an unknown path resolves to empty text with the published log line.

Run result announcements
The Run updates region announces each run's start, wait, success, failure and cancellation in the published sentences, once per transition.

Step list keyboard navigation
The step list on a run detail is navigable by keyboard in execution order, and Enter on an item opens that step's log with focus returning on close.

Loop over table rows
A loop over all rows of a seeded table adds one row per item to a second table, and the new rows are visible on the table screen and through the tables API.

Loop variables
Inside a loop body the loop index counts from 1 and the loop item gives the current item, and a body step's log holds one attempt line per iteration.

Step limit failure
A run that would exceed the step limit fails with the published message, skips the step that would exceed it and every later step that has not run, and is announced as failed.

Loop source rules
A loop whose list does not resolve to a list fails that step with the published message, and a loop over all rows of a table sees each row as an object with its row id.

Depth-first execution order
Steps run one at a time in the published depth-first order, with several edges on one port running in data-order and each downstream part finishing before the next.

Wait holds a run until the server clock
A run held by a wait step stays waiting until the workspace clock reaches its due time, then resumes and finishes, whatever the open tab's clock says.

Waiting run appears live
A collaborator's open run list shows a run as waiting, and later as succeeded, without a reload.

Cancelling a waiting run
Cancelling a waiting run by keyboard marks the waiting step cancelled and every unrun step skipped, and later clock advances never resume it.

Finished runs refuse cancel
Cancelling a run that has already finished is refused with the published status and body.

Browser clock never decides
With the browser's clock set hours away, run and step statuses, due times and times of day on screen show what the server pushes.

Retrying step journey
A failing call-webhook step shows retrying between attempts while the workspace clock is advanced, then follows its error edge to a send-email step or fails the run, with a collaborator watching live.

Attempt log lines
Every attempt of a step writes the published log line, and the attempt count and delay come from the published retry settings.

Error edge keeps the step failed
A step that fails after its last attempt follows its error edge, stays failed, and the run ends succeeded when nothing else fails.

Run failure without an error edge
A step that fails after its last attempt with no error edge fails the run with the published run message and skips every step not yet run.

Mail outage on send-email
With the mail service down, a send-email step retries on the workspace clock and then takes its error path or fails the run, and is never reported succeeded.

Export and import journey
A Workspace owner exports an automation by keyboard, imports the downloaded file, and lands on the new automation's editor with the same steps.

Export bytes match storage
An export is marked saved only after storage confirms it, and the object under the published key holds exactly the bytes the download gave.

Export format and import validation
The exported file has the published keys, and an import that names an unknown node kind or is not a Switchyard automation is refused with the published 422 message and stores nothing.

Import stored as uploaded
A valid import is stored under its published key byte for byte as uploaded and creates a new draft that lands the owner on its editor route.

Storage outage on export and import
With storage down, export and import answer the published 503 and show the published outage notice, nothing is marked saved, and health reports unavailable.

Webhook intake journey
With the run list open, a webhook delivery starts one run that appears live, a repeated delivery with the same key and body adds no row, and arrivals are announced.

Webhook refusal order
Webhook deliveries are refused in the published order of unknown path, wrong method, oversized body, wrong content type and malformed JSON, each with its published status and body.

Webhook body limit boundary
A body exactly at the webhook body limit starts a run, and a body one byte over is refused as too large and starts none.

Idempotent webhook replay and conflict
The same Idempotency-Key with the same body returns the original run without starting another, and the same key with a different body is refused.

Idempotency window on the workspace clock
A key is remembered for the published window measured on the workspace clock, after which the same key starts a new run.

Schedule journey
A Run operator watches scheduled runs appear in the run list in the workspace time zone as the workspace clock advances across a spring-forward day, a fall-back day and an interval schedule, and reads them on a phone.

Spring-forward daily schedule
A daily schedule at a wall-clock time that does not exist on the spring-forward day fires once at the next existing minute.

Fall-back daily schedule
A daily schedule at a repeated wall-clock time fires once on the fall-back day, at its first occurrence.

Interval schedule
An every-N-minutes schedule fires once per interval as the clock advances, each firing is its own run, and only the live version's schedule fires.

Workspace time zone display
Run start times, schedule times and due times show in the workspace time zone in the published format, whatever zone the browser is in.

Version pinning journey
A version 1 run asleep in a wait step finishes on version 1 after version 2 is published, while a new run uses version 2.

Versions are immutable and drain
Published versions never change, and each superseded version is draining while it has unfinished runs and retired when it has none.

Version numeral and drain counter
The canvas header shows the live version numeral and the drain counter, both taken from server records, and the counter changing is announced.

Run tokens and ghost edges
Each in-progress run is a token on the step it is at, runs on older versions keep a ghost of that version's edges and show their version, and the ghost edges disappear when the counter reaches zero.

Version drain motion
On publish the numeral steps from the old to the new version in the published animation, and reduced motion shows the final state at once while the counter still updates and is announced.

Co-editing journey
Two editors in separate browsers see each other's presence, one save wins and the other is refused live, the hold lapses on the workspace clock, and all of it works by keyboard.

Presence notice
Members on the same draft see the published presence notice, pushed when another member opens or leaves it.

Held step refuses another member
A save to a step held by another member is refused with the published conflict notice naming the holder, and the field shows the holder's value.

Hold lapses on the workspace clock
After the edit hold has lapsed on the workspace clock any member's save wins, and the previous holder sees it in place.

Simultaneous first saves
When two members save a fresh step at the same moment, exactly one save wins, the one the server received first.

Live run list by status
A run list filtered to failed receives a failing run live and ignores a succeeding one, with no reload.

Test runs hidden by default
A test run on sample data shows Draft, the Test chip and the test marker, and appears in the run list only while Show test runs is on.

Streams stay in the workspace
The live stream and every list, count and run detail carry only the member's workspace, and another workspace's runs never appear.

Filters by keyboard and announced
The run list filters work by keyboard and announce the shown count in the Run list results region.

Replay journey
A Run operator replays a seeded failed run from its failed step and lands on the new run, whose earlier steps are reused and which sends no second email.

Replay reuses recorded outputs
A replay creates a new run on the original's version, links to the original, and shows every earlier step reused with its recorded output.

Replay refusals
Replay is refused for a run that is not failed, for a start step after the failed step, and for a start step inside a loop.

Replay landing and announcement
After Replay the page lands on the new run's route and the new run is announced as started.

Replay by keyboard and live to others
The replay control is reachable and operable by keyboard, and a viewer in another browser sees the replay arrive in the run list live.

Phone step list
Below the canvas breakpoint the canvas is replaced by an ordered step list with the same step ids, kinds and statuses, and resizing above it brings the canvas back.

Step log by touch
Tapping a step opens its log with status, input, output, attempts and timing, and a tap on the close button closes it.

Breakpoint exactness
The canvas shows at the breakpoint width and above and the step list shows one pixel below it.

Touch targets and no sideways scroll
On a phone every control is large enough to tap as published, the page does not scroll sideways, and reduced motion shows version numerals and edges without animation.

Invite journey
A Workspace owner invites a viewer by email, the viewer opens the Mailpit link in another browser and lands on the workspace route, and sees the automations and runs read-only.

Viewer refusals
A viewer's edit, publish, run, import, export and invite are refused by the server with the published 403 body, and the controls are present but disabled with the published reason.

Other workspaces answer not found
A workspace, automation, run or table outside the member's workspaces answers 404 in the API and shows the not-found page by address.

Not-found page
The not-found page shows the published copy and its action for any unknown address.

Invite and sign-up email
Sign-up confirmation and member invites go out through Mailpit with the published subject and link, and answer the published 503 when the mail service is down.

Landing hero and example tabs
The signed-out landing page shows the release notice bar, the pill nav, a headline that builds letter by letter, and a preview frame whose three tabs swap three example automations, with no animation under reduced motion.

Working screens carry the visual language
Run lists, forms, tables, empty states and error states use the same dotted ground, pill nav, pink pill actions, dark rounded panels and typefaces as the landing page.

Canvas and step nodes
The editor canvas is a dark dotted panel of square step nodes on a snapping grid joined by dashed curved edges between ports, with status chips on run views.

Layouts at the three viewports
Each screen shows its published layout and element order at 375x812, 768x1024 and 1280x800 with no horizontal overflow.

Deployment manifest and health
The run manifest installs, builds and serves the app on the published port, and the health route answers as published for the primary and for each outage instance.

Grading routes
The grading setup and clock routes require the grading key, answer 404 without it, create what the request names, and move one workspace's clock, answering only after every due timer owned by the instance called has fired.

Run state survives restart
Drafts, versions, runs, step records, timers, idempotency keys and clock offsets survive a server restart, and waiting runs still resume at their due times.

Credentials from environment
Every service credential and URL is read from the published environment variables and is never hard-coded or sent to the browser.

Engine rules decided once
The run engine's status transitions, retry rule, step limit and version binding are each decided in one place in the source.
/app/run.json is a JSON object with string install, build and serve and "_schema":"run-manifest-v1".

THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md at the app root lists every shipped package (the production dependency tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json) with name, version and licence, and every bundled font file with its licence.
Shipped packages and bundled fonts carry only MIT, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, ISC or SIL OFL 1.1 licences.
No datastore, cache, queue or database file exists beyond Postgres and MinIO, and the automation engine runs inside the app server.
Neither the server nor the browser makes any network request at runtime except to the app itself, Postgres, MinIO and the mail server; fonts and images are bundled.
The service definitions and dev credentials supplied with the task are left untouched, and the app reads every credential from the environment.
A lockfile is committed and install uses it, with no step that downloads anything outside the package registry.
User-visible copy, routes and role names never call an automation or a run a "workflow", "flow" or "zap", and the product contains no AI feature.
